verdict.rationale: OpenCode's GitHub integration lets you ask it to fix an issue/feature and it works in a new branch and submits a PR (opencode-docs-12), which implies some background/autonomous task execution, and 'opencode serve' can run a headless server accessible remotely (opencode-docs-30, opencode-comm-7). However, there is no documented dedicated isolated cloud sandbox/VM for background task execution—the GitHub flow's execution environment isn't described as an isolated cloud sandbox, and self-hosting 'serve' just exposes your own machine's process, which community evidence even flags as an unauthenticated local-exec risk (opencode-comm-18). Missing for 10: explicit first-party isolated cloud execution environment for background agents, sandbox isolation guarantees, and independent confirmation of long-running background task reliability in the cloud.
